subject: Chemistry
prompt: Lucas test: tertiary alcohol reacts with Lucas reagent
explain: 3° alcohol reacts immediately with ZnCl₂/conc.HCl giving turbidity due to 3° carbocation stability.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Victor Meyer test: primary alcohol gives which colour?
explain: 1° alcohol → RCH₂NO₂ → pseudonitrole → red colour with HNO₂ and KOH.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Boiling point order: alcohol vs ether of same molecular formula
explain: Alcohols have intermolecular H-bonding, raising BP significantly above isomeric ethers.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Phenol acidity vs ethanol: which is stronger acid?
explain: Phenoxide ion is resonance-stabilised; phenol Ka ≈ 10⁻¹⁰, ethanol Ka ≈ 10⁻¹⁶.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Reaction of phenol with NaOH gives
explain: Phenol is acidic enough to react with NaOH (but not Na₂CO₃) forming sodium phenoxide.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Kolbe's reaction: phenol + CO₂/NaOH under pressure gives
explain: Kolbe's synthesis: sodium phenoxide + CO₂ → sodium salicylate → salicylic acid on acidification.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Reimer-Tiemann reaction introduces which group into phenol?
explain: Phenol + CHCl₃/NaOH → salicylaldehyde (ortho-hydroxybenzaldehyde) via dichlorocarbene.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Cleavage of ether by HI: which bond breaks in Ph–O–CH₃?
explain: For aryl alkyl ethers, HI cleaves the alkyl–O bond (SN2 on methyl) giving phenol + CH₃I.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Dehydration of alcohol at 443 K (170°C) with conc. H₂SO₄ gives
explain: Higher temperature (443 K) favours E2 elimination giving alkene; 413 K favours ether formation.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Dehydration of alcohol at 413 K with conc. H₂SO₄ gives
explain: At 413 K (140°C) with excess alcohol, intermolecular dehydration gives symmetrical ether (SN2).

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Oxidation of primary alcohol with PCC (pyridinium chlorochromate) gives
explain: PCC in CH₂Cl₂ oxidises 1° alcohol to aldehyde without over-oxidation to acid.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Oxidation of secondary alcohol with K₂Cr₂O₇/H₂SO₄ gives
explain: 2° alcohols are oxidised to ketones; ketones resist further oxidation under mild acidic conditions.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Tertiary alcohol on oxidation with K₂Cr₂O₇/H₂SO₄ (mild)
explain: 3° alcohols have no α-H for oxidation; they resist mild oxidising agents.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Phenol reacts with Br₂ water (without catalyst) giving
explain: –OH activates ring strongly; aqueous Br₂ (no catalyst) gives 2,4,6-tribromophenol as white ppt.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Nitration of phenol with dilute HNO₃ gives mainly
explain: –OH is ortho/para director; dilute HNO₃ gives mixture of o- and p-nitrophenol.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Picric acid is the common name for
explain: Picric acid = 2,4,6-trinitrophenol; strong acid (pKa ≈ 0.38) due to three –NO₂ groups.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: FeCl₃ test for phenol gives which colour?
explain: Phenol forms a violet-coloured complex with FeCl₃ due to Fe³⁺ coordination with phenoxide.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Williamson synthesis produces ethers via
explain: Sodium alkoxide (nucleophile) attacks alkyl halide by SN2; methyl/primary halides preferred.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: For Williamson synthesis, why can't 3° alkyl halide be used?
explain: Strong alkoxide base + 3° alkyl halide → favours E2 (Zaitsev elimination) instead of SN2.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Ethers are cleaved by HI more readily than HCl because
options: I⁻ is better nucleophile & HI stronger acid
explain: I⁻ is a stronger nucleophile (better SN2) and HI is stronger acid, providing more H⁺ for protonation.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Order of reactivity of alcohols with HX: which is fastest?
explain: Reactivity with HX follows carbocation stability: 3° > 2° > 1° (SN1 pathway for higher alcohols).

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Anisole (methoxybenzene) undergoes EAS at which position preferentially?
explain: –OCH₃ is ortho/para director (electron donor by resonance) activating ring at o- and p- positions.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which alcohol gives iodoform test positive?
explain: Iodoform test positive for CH₃CH(OH)– or CH₃CHO structure; ethanol (oxidised to acetaldehyde) qualifies.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Methanol is distinguished from ethanol by iodoform test because
explain: Methanol lacks CH₃C(OH)– unit; iodoform test negative for methanol, positive for ethanol.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Cresols are methyl-substituted phenols; how many isomers exist?
explain: Cresols (methylphenols) have three isomers: ortho-, meta-, and para-cresol.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Phenol reacts with Zn dust to give?
explain: Zinc dust reduces phenol by removing the –OH group, yielding benzene.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Phenol + conc. HNO₃/H₂SO₄ gives?
explain: Concentrated HNO₃ nitrates phenol at all three activated positions giving picric acid (2,4,6-trinitrophenol).

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which has higher boiling point: 1-propanol or 1-butanol?
explain: Higher molecular mass → stronger London dispersion forces → higher BP for 1-butanol.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Acid strength order among phenols: p-nitrophenol vs phenol?
explain: Electron-withdrawing –NO₂ stabilises phenoxide ion by resonance, increasing acidity.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Ethanol reacts with conc. H₂SO₄ at room temp to give?
explain: At low temperature, H₂SO₄ protonates ethanol forming ethyl hydrogen sulphate (esterification, no dehydration).

subject: Chemistry
prompt: What is the IUPAC name of anisole?
explain: Anisole = C₆H₅–O–CH₃; IUPAC name is methoxybenzene.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Phenol on treatment with acetyl chloride gives?
explain: Acylation of phenol's –OH with CH₃COCl forms phenyl acetate (ester), releasing HCl.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which reagent converts primary alcohol directly to aldehyde without over-oxidation?
explain: PCC (mild oxidant) halts oxidation at aldehyde stage; aqueous oxidants go on to carboxylic acid.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Glycerol is chemically known as?
explain: Glycerol has three –OH groups on a 3-carbon chain; IUPAC: propane-1,2,3-triol.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Diethyl ether reacts with excess HI to give?
explain: Excess HI cleaves both C–O bonds of ether, converting both ethyl groups to ethyl iodide.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: In Williamson synthesis, sodium alkoxide acts as?
explain: RO⁻ (alkoxide) attacks alkyl halide via SN2; it is the nucleophile in the reaction.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Coupling reaction of phenol with diazonium salt gives?
explain: Electrophilic diazonium ion attacks phenol ring at para position forming orange/red azo dye.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Ethylene glycol is used as antifreeze because?
options: It lowers freezing point of water
It raises boiling point of fuel
explain: Ethylene glycol (diol) is miscible with water and lowers its freezing point via colligative effect.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which alcohol cannot be oxidised to an aldehyde or ketone?
explain: Tertiary alcohols have no α-H on the carbon bearing –OH, so they resist mild oxidation.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Phenol is more acidic than alcohol because phenoxide ion is?
explain: Negative charge on phenoxide delocalises over the ring (resonance), stabilising it far more than alkoxide.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Reaction of phenol with CHCl₃ + NaOH (Reimer-Tiemann) at high temp gives?
explain: Classic Reimer-Tiemann: CHCl₃/NaOH introduces –CHO group ortho to –OH giving salicylaldehyde.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Oxymercuration–demercuration of alkene gives which type of alcohol?
explain: Oxymercuration follows Markovnikov's rule: –OH adds to the more substituted carbon.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which functional group makes ethers relatively unreactive to bases?
explain: Ethers lack acidic –OH and carbonyl group; C–O–C is stable to bases, making ethers inert to NaOH.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Crown ethers are cyclic polyethers; they preferentially complex?
explain: Crown ether cavity size matches alkali metal cation radii; O-lone pairs coordinate the cation.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Hydroboration–oxidation of propene gives which alcohol?
explain: Hydroboration is anti-Markovnikov: –OH goes to less substituted carbon giving 1-propanol.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Phenol undergoes sulphonation with conc. H₂SO₄ at room temp to give mainly?
explain: At low temperature, kinetic (ortho) product predominates in electrophilic sulphonation of phenol.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which product forms when diethyl ether is exposed to air and light over time?
explain: Auto-oxidation of ether α-C–H by O₂ (free-radical) forms dangerous diethyl peroxide on standing.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Propan-2-ol on oxidation with acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ gives?
explain: Secondary alcohol → ketone upon oxidation; propan-2-ol gives propanone (acetone).

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Baeyer's reagent (cold KMnO₄/OH⁻) converts alkene to?
explain: Cold alkaline KMnO₄ adds two –OH groups syn across double bond, forming a vicinal diol.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: The C–O bond length in phenol compared to aliphatic alcohols is?
explain: Resonance delocalises lone pair of O into ring, giving C–O partial double bond character → shorter bond.
